title: Affine denominator maps are injective on a full-support module without embedded primes
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and M a finite A-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] whose support is Spec(A) and whose associated primes are all minimal primes of A. Let a and b be non-zero-divisors of A, let q be the localization of A at the multiplicative set of all non-zero-divisors (the total quotient ring), and put I = {x in A | x(a/b) belongs to A inside q}. Then I is an ideal of A (and hence is finitely generated), multiplication gives an injective A-linear map I M \to M, and the rule x m \mapsto (a/b)(x m), interpreted in the localization M_b and using that b is a non-zero-divisor on M, gives an injective A-linear map I M \to M. The cokernel of the first map is annihilated by I, and the cokernel of the second map is annihilated by the submodule (a/b)I of A.

source.place: Tag 02P2 (Lemma 31.25.5), affine proof after writing s=a/b

proof.text: Since A embeds in its total quotient ring Q, the equation c=(a/b)x in Q is equivalent to bc=ax in A: multiply by b, using that its image is a unit. Define I as the inverse image under multiplication by a of the range of multiplication by b, and J as the inverse image under multiplication by b of the range of multiplication by a. These are actual ideals, with x in I iff there exists c with bc=ax, and c in J iff there exists x in I with bc=ax. Thus they have exactly the required denominator membership descriptions. I is finitely generated because A is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 02P2 proof, definition of I and Noetherian finite generation

proof.text: A non-zero-divisor c of A lies in no minimal prime by [lem-pc-minimal-prime-avoids-nonzerodivisor]. The hypothesis on associated primes therefore shows that c lies in no associated prime of M. Using the equivalent regular-element form biUnion_associatedPrimes_eq_compl_regular of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes], multiplication by c is injective on M. Apply this to a and b. Every power of b also acts injectively, so IsLocalizedModule.injective_iff_isRegular gives injectivity of M to M_b.

proof.text: Put N=IM and B=(multiplication by b on M). For x in I choose c with bc=ax. Then a(xm)=b(cm) lies in range(B). Induction over the sums of generators xm of IM proves aN is contained in range(B). The inverse of the injective linear map B onto its range, composed with multiplication by a on N, gives an A-linear map f:N to M with bf(z)=az. This is the unique division map of the source, since b is injective. If f(z)=f(w), multiply by b and cancel the injective action of a to deduce z=w. The first map is the submodule inclusion and is injective.

proof.text: For i in I and m in M, im belongs to IM, hence is in the range of its inclusion N to M. The annihilator-of-quotient criterion Submodule.annihilator_quotient therefore gives I contained in the annihilator of the first cokernel.

source.place: Tag 02P2 proof, final sentence on M/IM

proof.text: If c is in J, choose x in I with bc=ax. For every m in M, injectivity of b and the defining equation of f give f(xm)=cm: both sides become axm after multiplication by b. Thus cm lies in range(f). The same annihilator-of-quotient criterion gives J contained in the annihilator of the second cokernel.

lean.statement: theorem hilbert_affine_denominator_module (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (hSupport : Module.support A M = Set.univ) (hAssoc : associatedPrimes A M ⊆ minimalPrimes A) (a b : A) (ha : a ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (hb : b ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) : let Q := Localization (nonZeroDivisors A) let s : Q := IsLocalization.mk' Q a ⟨b, hb⟩ ∃ (I J : Ideal A), (∀ x : A, x ∈ I ↔ ∃ c : A, algebraMap A Q c = s * algebraMap A Q x) ∧ I.FG ∧ (∀ c : A, c ∈ J ↔ ∃ x ∈ I, algebraMap A Q c = s * algebraMap A Q x) ∧ IsSMulRegular M b ∧ Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers b) M) ∧ let N : Submodule A M := I • (⊤ : Submodule A M) Function.Injective N.subtype ∧ ∃ f : N →ₗ[A] M, (∀ z : N, b • f z = a • (z : M)) ∧ Function.Injective f ∧ I ≤ Module.annihilator A (M ⧸ LinearMap.range N.subtype) ∧ J ≤ Module.annihilator A (M ⧸ LinearMap.range f)
